# Requirements Document: Changing an order item

## Introduction

An order item is never changed in place.  A change replaces the item with a
new one: the services the change keeps move to the new item under the same
references, and their copies in the original item are marked transferred.
The other services of the original item are cancelled.  This is the change
once it is paid, as the worked examples show it after payment.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Change/Transfer.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Change/Transfer.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-204

**User Story:** As an airline, I want a changed item's kept services to move to the new item under the same references, so that each service is delivered and accounted for once.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller has accepted and paid a change to an order item THE SYSTEM SHALL add a new item with the services the change keeps and cancel the services it does not keep. (Lean: `changeItem`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a change keeps a service of the changed item THE SYSTEM SHALL give the new item a service with the same reference, passenger, segment and delivery status.
   - ONE-204.1, proven: proven theorem `change_keeps_services`; example `changeKeepingOutbound`
2. WHEN a change keeps a service of the changed item THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the original copy transferred and leave its delivery status as it was.
   - ONE-204.2, proven: proven theorem `change_marks_transferred`; example `changeKeepingOutbound`
3. WHEN a change does not keep a service of the changed item and the delivery status table lets it be removed THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it cancelled and removed.
   - ONE-204.3, proven: proven theorem `change_cancels_others`; example `changeAfterOutboundFlown`; example `changeKeepingOutbound`; example `changeReplacingAll`
4. WHEN a change is made THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order's item references distinct.
   - ONE-204.4, proven: proven theorem `change_item_refs_unique`; example `changeReusingReference`
5. WHEN a change is made THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the changed item cancelled.
   - ONE-204.5, open: open theorem `change_original_cancelled`; counterexample `changeKeepingOutbound`

#### Open question on ONE-204.5

> After a change, the changed item is cancelled, under every reading of the
> guide.
>
> Open question for the business.  The worked examples leave the transferred
> copies in the changed item READY TO PROCEED and show the item CANCELLED.  The
> guide's item status rule judges value by delivery status alone, and a service
> READY TO PROCEED holds value under every reading, so the changed item stays
> active and the kept service holds value in both items.  The example
> `changeKeepingOutbound` shows it.  Does the TRANSFERRED status take away a
> service's value, or should the original copy move to a delivery status that
> holds none?
